We find that BUG integrators, due to their reduced numerical cost and the flexibility of the concept, provide a competitive and, in certain regimes, advantageous alternative to the well-established time-stepping by projector-splitting in TDVP, especially in models with large local dimensions, and in cases where observables are extracted with high temporal resolution.

AI.tldr: This work formulates two Basis Update and Galerkin (BUG) integrators for matrix product states (MPS) as an alternative to projector-splitting TDVP, showing competitive and sometimes advantageous performance.
AI.motivation: Simulating nonequilibrium dynamics in strongly correlated quantum systems via tensor-network time evolution is challenging. Projector-splitting TDVP is the gold standard but has limitations; a more flexible alternative is desired.
AI.method: Two BUG integrators (first-order augmented and second-order midpoint) are formulated explicitly for MPS, yielding single-site integrators robust to small singular values, avoiding backward-in-time substeps, and enabling adaptive bond dimensions. Their relation to projector-splitting TDVP is clarified.
AI.result: Systematic numerical comparisons on the long-range XY spin model and 2D fermion/spin lattice models show BUG integrators reduce numerical cost and offer competitive accuracy, especially for large local dimensions and high temporal resolution observables.
AI.conclusion: Due to reduced cost and conceptual flexibility, BUG integrators provide a competitive and in some regimes advantageous alternative to projector-splitting time-stepping in TDVP.

title: On energy equality of the 3D anisotropic Navier-Stokes equations
summary: In the spirit of the recent work by Demmel and Wiedemann \cite{[DW]}, we investigate the validity of the energy balance law for weak solutions to the three-dimensional Navier-Stokes equations with only horizontal dissipation. We prove that famous Lions-Shinbrot type energy conservation criteria, originally established for the classical isotropic Navier-Stokes equations, continue to hold in this anisotropic setting. Furthermore, we present two distinct approaches that handle the torus case and the whole space case, respectively.

AI.tldr: The paper proves that Lions-Shinbrot-type energy conservation criteria for weak solutions to the 3D Navier-Stokes equations remain valid in the anisotropic setting with only horizontal dissipation, using two approaches for the torus and whole-space cases.
AI.motivation: Motivated by recent work of Demmel and Wiedemann, the authors examine whether the energy balance law holds for weak solutions of the 3D Navier-Stokes equations when dissipation acts only in the horizontal directions.
AI.method: The authors extend classical Lions-Shinbrot energy conservation criteria to the anisotropic (horizontally dissipated) Navier-Stokes equations, developing two distinct analytical approaches to handle the torus case and the whole space case separately.
AI.result: They establish that the famous Lions-Shinbrot-type energy conservation criteria continue to hold in the anisotropic setting despite the reduced dissipation.
AI.conclusion: Energy conservation criteria known for isotropic Navier-Stokes equations extend to the horizontally dissipated anisotropic case, with separate techniques required for the torus and whole space.

title: Normal Equations and Discrete Energy Structures for High-Order Streamline Diffusion
summary: We analyse fully discrete Streamline Diffusion finite element methods, also known as SUPG methods, for time-dependent first-order systems with skew-symmetric spatial operators. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first stability and a priori error analysis of strongly consistent Streamline Diffusion finite elements combined with linear multistep schemes of order greater than two for multidimensional first-order hyperbolic systems. Local-in-time $L^2$-residual minimisation singles out $δ=b_0τ$, where $δ$ is the stabilisation parameter, $τ$ the time step, and $b_0$ the current-time coefficient in the method average. For this choice, each implicit linear system is a symmetric positive definite normal equation in a graph norm. A direct dual-residual estimate yields errors of order $O(h^{k+1/2}+τ^ν)$ when $δ$ is proportional to $h$ and $τ=O(h)$, where $h$ is the mesh size, $k$ the polynomial degree, and $ν$ the temporal order. Stability is established for the $θ$-method and the Adams-Moulton methods AM3-AM5. The general-degree AM3 and AM4 estimates use strengthened CFL conditions; for continuous piecewise affine elements, an elementwise cancellation recovers the standard hyperbolic regime. AM5 and the explicit Adams-Bashforth methods AB3 and AB4 are stable under a standard hyperbolic CFL condition, though the explicit schemes do not have normal-equation structure. Order-matched acoustic tests recover orders two through five and material-residual rates one half-order lower. In a d'Alembert test with discontinuous initial data, normal-equation SUPG recovers second-order local $\mathbb P_1$ convergence away from the wave fronts, whereas the unstabilised error is close to half order. A two-dimensional compact-wave test shows improved localisation with modest dissipation.

AI.tldr: First stability and a priori error analysis of strongly consistent Streamline Diffusion (SUPG) finite elements combined with high-order linear multistep schemes for multidimensional first-order hyperbolic systems, with a stable choice of the stabilisation parameter.
AI.motivation: Streamline Diffusion/SUPG methods for time-dependent first-order systems with skew-symmetric spatial operators lacked a stability and a priori error analysis when combined with linear multistep schemes of order greater than two, especially in the multidimensional case.
AI.method: Fully discrete SUPG finite elements coupled with linear multistep time integration. Local-in-time L2-residual minimisation selects the stabilisation parameter δ=b0τ (τ=time step, b0=current-time coefficient in the method average), making each implicit linear system a symmetric positive definite normal equation in a graph norm. A direct dual-residual estimate derives the error bounds.
AI.result: Errors of order O(h^{k+1/2}+τ^ν) for δ ∝ h and τ=O(h) (h mesh size, k polynomial degree, ν temporal order). Stability for the θ-method and Adams-Moulton AM3-AM5; general-degree AM3/AM4 need strengthened CFL conditions, while continuous piecewise affine elements recover the standard hyperbolic regime via elementwise cancellation. AM5, AB3, AB4 are stable under a standard hyperbolic CFL condition. Acoustic tests recover orders two through five; material-residual rates one half-order lower. In a d'Alembert test with discontinuous data, normal-equation SUPG recovers second-order local P1 convergence away from wave fronts (vs. ~half-order unstabilised). A 2D compact-wave test shows improved localisation with modest dissipation.
AI.conclusion: The stable δ=b0τ normal-equation SUPG formulation provides provable high-order accuracy and stability for multidimensional first-order hyperbolic systems, with numerical tests confirming the predicted convergence orders and improved localisation.

title: Extreme-Scale Linear-Scaling Kohn-Sham DFT at 100 Million Atoms: Bridging Quantum Simulations and Experiments
comment: 12 pages, 6 figures; submitted to SC26 (The International Conference for High Performance Computing, Networking, Storage, and Analysis)
summary: Kohn-Sham density functional theory (DFT) remains the workhorse of ab initio materials simulation, yet cubic computational and quadratic memory scaling have confined calculations to a few hundred to thousands of atoms, spanning only nanometers, far below experimentally relevant length scales. We introduce XLSDFT, a linear-scaling DFT framework based on divide-and-conquer decomposition of the one-particle density matrix and Chebyshev-filtered subspace iteration, achieving linear computational and memory scaling while retaining DFT accuracy. Deployed on the LineShine exascale supercomputer, XLSDFT reduces computational complexity by orders of magnitude, enabling unprecedented DFT scale: a 200-million-atom silicon crystal, twentyfold beyond the prior record. Our implementation achieves 96.6% weak-scaling efficiency and sustained 157.9 Pflop/s (FP64) for a 100-million-atom scaling study. We further simulate an 11-million-atom all-solid-state battery interface of unprecedented complexity, 1,000 times beyond prior DFT for such systems, revealing how lithium metal reacts with the solid electrolyte at atomic resolution, in quantitative agreement with spectroscopy experiments.

AI.tldr: XLSDFT is a linear-scaling Kohn-Sham DFT framework using divide-and-conquer density matrix decomposition and Chebyshev-filtered subspace iteration, enabling a 200-million-atom silicon calculation and a realistic solid-state battery interface simulation on an exascale supercomputer.
AI.motivation: Conventional Kohn-Sham DFT suffers from cubic computational and quadratic memory scaling, limiting simulations to a few hundred to thousands of atoms (nanometer scale), far below experimentally relevant length scales.
AI.method: XLSDFT combines divide-and-conquer decomposition of the one-particle density matrix with Chebyshev-filtered subspace iteration to achieve linear computational and memory scaling while preserving DFT accuracy. It was deployed on the LineShine exascale supercomputer.
AI.result: The framework reduces computational complexity by orders of magnitude, simulating a 200-million-atom silicon crystal (twentyfold beyond the prior record) with 96.6% weak-scaling efficiency and sustained 157.9 Pflop/s (FP64) for a 100-million-atom study. It also simulated an 11-million-atom all-solid-state battery interface (1,000x beyond prior DFT for such systems), revealing lithium metal reactivity with the solid electrolyte at atomic resolution, matching spectroscopy experiments.
AI.conclusion: XLSDFT demonstrates that linear-scaling DFT on exascale hardware can reach experimentally relevant length scales, enabling atomic-resolution, quantitatively accurate simulation of complex realistic interfaces previously inaccessible to DFT.

title: Scattering Across the Long-Range Threshold for One-Dimensional Nonlinear Schrödinger Equations
summary: We study small solutions to the one-dimensional nonlinear Schrödinger family \[ \mathrm{i}\partial_t u_δ=-\partial_x^2u_δ+κ|u_δ|^{2+δ}u_δ, \qquad 0\leqδ\leqδ_0, \] uniformly as $δ\to0^+$ and $t\to\infty$, across the threshold between cubic modified scattering and nearby-power ordinary scattering. For initial data small in $H^{0,1}(\mathbb{R})$, with one spatial weight and no physical derivative assumed, we prove a joint-limit asymptotic formula governed by an explicit nonlinear clock. The variable $ δ\log t$ gives three regimes according as it tends to zero, a positive finite limit, or infinity. Within the regime $δ\log t\to0$, successive Taylor terms of the clock become visible at an infinite hierarchy of time scales, each requiring finer absolute phase accuracy. These scales accumulate at the transition scale, where the exact clock describes them together. In the transition and saturated regimes, the clock is of order $δ^{-1}$, so the first-order variation of its coefficient contributes a finite phase correction.

AI.tldr: Small $H^{0,1}$ solutions to a 1D nonlinear Schrödinger family $i\partial_t u_\delta=-\partial_x^2 u_\delta+\kappa|u_\delta|^{2+\delta}u_\delta$ are analyzed uniformly as $\delta\to0^+$ and $t\to\infty$, bridging cubic modified scattering and nearby-power ordinary scattering via an explicit nonlinear clock.
AI.motivation: The paper addresses the threshold between cubic modified scattering and nearby-power ordinary scattering in the 1D NLS family, seeking a uniform asymptotic description as the nonlinearity exponent approaches cubic ($\delta\to0^+$) and time goes to infinity.
AI.method: For small $H^{0,1}(\mathbb{R})$ data with one spatial weight and no physical derivative assumed, the authors derive a joint-limit asymptotic formula governed by an explicit nonlinear clock, analyzing the three regimes determined by $\delta\log t$ (tending to zero, a positive finite limit, or infinity).
AI.result: In the regime $\delta\log t\to0$, successive Taylor terms of the clock become visible at an infinite hierarchy of time scales, each needing finer absolute phase accuracy, accumulating at the transition scale where the exact clock describes them together. In the transition and saturated regimes, the clock is of order $\delta^{-1}$, so the first-order variation of its coefficient contributes a finite phase correction.
AI.conclusion: The work provides a unified description of small-data asymptotics across the cubic-to-nearby-power scattering threshold, with the nonlinear clock recovering modified scattering behavior at the transition and capturing an infinite hierarchy of time scales.

title: A parameterized block LU preconditioning for double saddle point problems
summary: We present a biparametric preconditioning technique for large, sparse, non-symmetric, and non-singular double saddle point problems. The preconditioner is induced using a stationary iteration method. It is also based on a two-parameterized block LU factorization of the coefficient matrix. To begin with, some convergence results of the iteration method are derived. Moreover, the spectral features exhibited by the preconditioned matrix are given. Finally, the presented preconditioner is conjuncted with the GMRES method. Numerical results demonstrate the satisfactory performance of the preconditioner.

AI.tldr: A biparametric preconditioner for large sparse non-symmetric double saddle point problems, derived from a stationary iteration and block LU factorization, with convergence and spectral analysis, tested with GMRES.
AI.motivation: Large, sparse, non-symmetric, non-singular double saddle point problems are difficult to solve efficiently; effective preconditioning is needed for iterative methods like GMRES.
AI.method: A biparametric preconditioning technique induced by a stationary iteration method and based on a two-parameterized block LU factorization of the coefficient matrix. Convergence results of the iteration and spectral properties of the preconditioned matrix are derived, and the preconditioner is combined with GMRES.
AI.result: Numerical results demonstrate satisfactory performance of the proposed preconditioner.
AI.conclusion: The biparametric preconditioner is effective for double saddle point problems when used with GMRES.

title: Regularity theory and low Mach number limit for the fractional Euler-alignment system
summary: We study the compressible Euler-alignment system with pressure under a singular pressure scaling, where the hypersingular communication weight induces a fractional alignment operator of order $2α$, $0<α<1$. The scaling corresponds to a large-time and small-velocity regime and leads to a low Mach number problem in which the density is forced to remain close to a constant state. Our main result is a uniform regularity theory for this scaled pressure system. We establish uniform estimates with respect to the scaling parameter and construct global strong solutions near the constant state. A key feature of the analysis is that, in the low-order fractional regime $0<α\le\frac12$, the estimates close under the lower Sobolev condition $s>\frac d2+1-2α$, gaining $α$ derivatives over the threshold $s>\frac d2 + 1 - α$ arising from a direct use of the fractional alignment dissipation. This is achieved by combining refined commutator estimates for the singular alignment operator with the density dissipation induced by the pressure scaling. As an application of the uniform estimates, we justify the low Mach number limit toward the incompressible Navier--Stokes system with fractional dissipation. For general small, possibly ill-prepared initial data, a Helmholtz decomposition combined with dispersive estimates for the acoustic component yields subsequential strong convergence locally in space-time to a distributional solution of the limiting system. For well-prepared initial data, a relative-energy argument further identifies the limit with a prescribed sufficiently regular solution and yields global strong convergence in the fractional dissipation norm.

AI.tldr: Uniform regularity theory and low Mach number limit for the compressible Euler-alignment system with singular pressure scaling and fractional alignment of order 2α.
AI.motivation: To understand compressible Euler-alignment systems in a large-time, small-velocity regime, where singular pressure scaling forces density near a constant state, and to rigorously justify the low Mach number limit toward incompressible Navier-Stokes with fractional dissipation.
AI.method: Combines refined commutator estimates for the singular fractional alignment operator with density dissipation from the pressure scaling; uses uniform estimates in the scaling parameter; a Helmholtz decomposition with dispersive acoustic estimates; and a relative-energy argument for well-prepared data.
AI.result: Establishes uniform estimates and global strong solutions near the constant state. In the low-order fractional regime 0<α≤1/2, closes estimates under the weaker condition s>d/2+1−2α, gaining α derivatives over the threshold s>d/2+1−α. Justifies the low Mach limit to incompressible Navier-Stokes: subsequential local strong convergence for ill-prepared data, and global strong convergence in the fractional dissipation norm for well-prepared data.
AI.conclusion: Provides a uniform regularity framework for the scaled singular pressure system and rigorously derives the incompressible fractional Navier-Stokes limit, with sharper Sobolev thresholds and different convergence results depending on data preparation.

title: Second-Order IMEX Time-Stepping Methods for Efficient Bidomain Multi-Electrode Array Simulations of Cardiac Stem Cell Monolayers
summary: Multi-electrode Arrays (MEAs) enable tissue-level electrophysiological studies of human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes (hiPSC-CMs) by recording extracellular field potentials. Recent computational models have improved MEA simulations by coupling detailed electrode descriptions with the Bidomain framework, a parabolic-elliptic system of nonlinear PDEs coupled with a stiff ionic model. The standard numerical strategy relies on operator splitting techniques that decouple the PDE and ODE components. In most implementations, the ionic subsystem is treated explicitly while the diffusive operator is handled implicitly, resulting in a first-order implicit-explicit (IMEX) time discretization. Although computationally convenient, this approach limits temporal accuracy and may reduce efficiency in large-scale simulations. In this work, we investigate higher-order IMEX Runge-Kutta schemes within a Strang-based operator splitting, specifically tailored for the MEA model of hiPSC-CMs monolayers. First- and second-order schemes are compared in terms of computational cost and global error against a high-fidelity reference solution obtained with a very small time step. For a fixed computational cost, the second-order schemes achieve errors that are 2-3 orders of magnitude smaller than those of the first-order method. These results demonstrate that higher-order IMEX integration significantly improves the accuracy-to-cost ratio of MEA simulations, providing a practical and reliable approach for large-scale electrophysiological studies.

AI.tldr: Higher-order IMEX Runge-Kutta schemes within Strang splitting improve accuracy-to-cost ratio in MEA simulations of hiPSC-CM monolayers, yielding 2-3 orders of magnitude lower error than first-order methods.
AI.motivation: Multi-electrode arrays enable tissue-level electrophysiology studies of hiPSC-CMs, and recent Bidomain-based MEA models couple detailed electrode descriptions with a parabolic-elliptic PDE system and stiff ionic ODE model. Standard operator splitting treats the ionic subsystem explicitly and the diffusive operator implicitly, giving only first-order IMEX discretization, which limits temporal accuracy and reduces efficiency in large-scale simulations.
AI.method: The authors investigate higher-order IMEX Runge-Kutta schemes within a Strang-based operator splitting, tailored to the MEA model of hiPSC-CM monolayers. First- and second-order schemes are compared in terms of computational cost and global error against a high-fidelity reference solution computed with a very small time step.
AI.result: For a fixed computational cost, the second-order schemes achieve errors 2-3 orders of magnitude smaller than the first-order method.
AI.conclusion: Higher-order IMEX integration significantly improves the accuracy-to-cost ratio of MEA simulations, offering a practical and reliable approach for large-scale electrophysiological studies.

title: Large-data modified wave operators for the defocusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation in one space dimension with subcritical long-range nonlinearity
summary: We study long-time behavior of the solutions to the final state problem for the defocusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation (NLS) in one space dimension with the power nonlinearity $|u|^{2σ}u$ in the subcritical long-range regime $\frac{2}{\sqrt{7}}<σ<1$. Given a prescribed asymptotic profile in a weighted $L^2$-space, without size restriction, obtained by modifying the free solution with a nonlinear polynomial phase correction, we construct a unique global solution of the NLS that scatters to this profile, thereby proving the existence of modified wave operators. The proof relies on two new ingredients. Extending our previous work for the cubic case, we incorporate the leading part of the nonlinear term into the linear part as a linear potential by linearizing the NLS around the asymptotic profile and prove a global modified energy estimate for the linearized equation. We also exploit a specific structure of the nonlinearity arising from the linearization, which gives rise to a crucial cancellation when estimating the nonlinear terms in the modified energy space and enables us to control the polynomial growth of the nonlinear phase correction in the subcritical case.

AI.tldr: The paper proves existence of modified wave operators for the defocusing 1D NLS with power nonlinearity |u|^{2σ}u in the subcritical long-range regime 2/√7 < σ < 1, constructing unique global solutions scattering to a prescribed modified asymptotic profile, without size restriction.
AI.motivation: Long-range nonlinearities prevent standard scattering; one needs modified wave operators with nonlinear phase corrections. Previous work only handled the cubic case (σ=1), leaving the wider subcritical long-range regime 2/√7 < σ < 1 open.
AI.method: Linearize the NLS around the modified asymptotic profile, absorbing the leading nonlinear part as a linear potential into the linear operator; prove a global modified energy estimate for the linearized equation; exploit a specific structure of the linearization-induced nonlinearity giving a crucial cancellation to control polynomial growth of the phase correction.
AI.result: Given any prescribed asymptotic profile in a weighted L²-space, modified by a nonlinear polynomial phase correction, a unique global solution of the NLS is constructed scattering to this profile, establishing existence of modified wave operators with no size restriction.
AI.conclusion: The approach extends the cubic-case method to the subcritical long-range regime, showing modified wave operators exist there; the key advances are the global modified energy estimate for the linearized equation and the cancellation controlling polynomial growth.

title: An Optimal IPDG Scheme for the Biharmonic Equation
summary: This paper presents an optimal interior penalty discontinuous Galerkin (IPDG) scheme for the planar biharmonic equation using piecewise polynomials of degree $k=3$ or $4$. In standard IPDG methods, large penalty parameters force the discrete solution into an overconstrained space, severely degrading accuracy---phenomenon known as numerical locking. To overcome this, our method enforces only vertex continuity and projects the jumps of the function and its normal derivative onto $\mathcal{P}^{k-3}$ and $\mathcal{P}^{k-2}$, respectively. Consequently, as the penalty parameters tend to infinity, the discrete solution is forced to lie in a constrained subspace $V_{h,\infty}^k$, which we identify as the optimal nonconforming finite element space $B_h^k$. This intrinsic connection fundamentally eliminates numerical locking. We prove optimal error estimates of $\mathcal{O}(h^{k-1})$ in a mesh-dependent energy norm and $\mathcal{O}(h^{k+1})$ in the $L^2$ norm. Numerical experiments on both convex and L-shaped domains confirm that the proposed scheme is robust and entirely locking-free, even for extremely large penalty parameters.

AI.tldr: An optimal interior penalty DG scheme for the planar biharmonic equation (k=3,4) that eliminates numerical locking by projecting jumps onto low-order polynomial spaces and connecting to an optimal nonconforming FE space.
AI.motivation: Standard IPDG methods suffer from numerical locking: large penalty parameters overconstrain the discrete solution and severely degrade accuracy. This work aims to overcome that limitation.
AI.method: The scheme enforces only vertex continuity and projects the jumps of the function and its normal derivative onto P^{k-3} and P^{k-2}, respectively. As penalty parameters go to infinity, the discrete solution lies in a constrained subspace V_{h,inf}^k, identified as the optimal nonconforming finite element space B_h^k.
AI.result: Optimal error estimates of O(h^{k-1}) in a mesh-dependent energy norm and O(h^{k+1}) in the L^2 norm. Numerical experiments on convex and L-shaped domains confirm robustness and full locking-freeness even for extremely large penalty parameters.
AI.conclusion: The intrinsic connection between the constrained subspace and the optimal nonconforming space fundamentally eliminates numerical locking, yielding an optimal, robust IPDG scheme for the biharmonic equation.

title: Least energy sign-changing solutions for asymptotically cubic Kirchhoff equations on locally finite graphs
summary: We obtain the existence results of least energy sign-changing solutions and ground state solutions for a class of asymptotically cubic Kirchhoff equations with Dirichlet boundary value on a locally finite graph $G=(V,E)$, and obtain the least energy of sign-changing solutions is strictly larger than twice of the ground state energy.

AI.tldr: The paper establishes existence of least energy sign-changing solutions and ground state solutions for asymptotically cubic Kirchhoff equations with Dirichlet boundary conditions on a locally finite graph, showing the sign-changing least energy strictly exceeds twice the ground state energy.
AI.motivation: Kirchhoff-type equations with Dirichlet boundary conditions on locally finite graphs are studied, addressing the asymptotically cubic case where existence and energy comparison results are sought.
AI.method: Variational methods on graphs, analyzing the Kirchhoff equation with Dirichlet boundary value on a locally finite graph G=(V,E).
AI.result: Least energy sign-changing solutions and ground state solutions are shown to exist. The least energy of sign-changing solutions is strictly larger than twice the ground state energy.
AI.conclusion: Existence of both solution types is confirmed, with a strict energy gap between sign-changing least energy and twice the ground state energy.

title: Total Generalized Variation for Inverse Problems Involving Piecewise Linear Finite Elements
summary: Higher-order regularization has shown improved results over first-order methods such as total variation. In this paper, convergence of a piecewise linear finite element discretization is shown for the second-order total generalized variation functional. Additionally, this convergence result is extended to a spatiotemporal setting after the spatiotemporal function space is comprehensively introduced. In both cases, discrete minimizers converge to the continuous minimizer with rate $h^{1/4}$, matching the best known rate for finite element discretizations of total variation in the same general setting. Numerical experiments confirm the convergence rates and indicate faster convergence in practice. Comparisons with related spatial image reconstruction algorithms show comparable reconstruction results. The spatiotemporal case is discussed using the example of the inverse problem in electrocardiographic imaging, where the proposed functional improves the state of the art.

AI.tldr: The paper proves convergence of a piecewise linear finite element discretization for the second-order total generalized variation (TGV) functional, extending it to a spatiotemporal setting, with rate h^{1/4} matching the best known rate for TV discretizations.
AI.motivation: Higher-order regularization like TGV improves on first-order methods such as total variation, but convergence of finite element discretizations for TGV was not established, especially in spatiotemporal settings.
AI.method: Piecewise linear finite element discretization of the second-order TGV functional; convergence analysis extended to a spatiotemporal framework after introducing the spatiotemporal function space.
AI.result: Discrete minimizers converge to the continuous minimizer at rate h^{1/4} in both cases, matching the best known TV rate; numerical experiments confirm the rates, show faster practical convergence, and comparable reconstruction to related algorithms; the spatiotemporal case improves state of the art in electrocardiographic imaging.
AI.conclusion: The discretization scheme is proven convergent with competitive rates, and the TGV functional provides improved results particularly for spatiotemporal inverse problems like electrocardiographic imaging.

title: On the Large $Λ$ Asymptotics of the One Phase Bernoulli Free Boundary Problem
summary: In this paper, we investigate the asymptotic behavior of minimizers $u_Λ$ of the Bernoulli functional $\int_D |\nabla v|^2 \, dx +Λ|Ω_v|$ for large $Λ$ with a boundary datum $g \ge 0$. In particular, in the case $g>0$, we show graphicality of the free boundary over $\partial D$ and obtain a second order asymptotic expansion in $Λ$ of the graph.

AI.tldr: The paper studies the asymptotic behavior, as the parameter Λ grows large, of minimizers of a Bernoulli-type functional with a nonnegative boundary datum, establishing graphicality of the free boundary and a second-order asymptotic expansion in Λ.
AI.motivation: Understanding minimizers of Bernoulli functionals is of interest in free boundary problems. The behavior for large Λ, particularly the geometric structure of the free boundary near the domain boundary, was not fully characterized.
AI.method: Asymptotic analysis of minimizers u_Λ of the functional ∫_D |∇v|^2 dx + Λ|Ω_v| subject to a boundary datum g ≥ 0, focusing on the large-Λ regime.
AI.result: For g > 0, the free boundary is shown to be graphical over ∂D, and a second-order asymptotic expansion in Λ of the graph is derived.
AI.conclusion: The minimizers exhibit controlled geometry (graphical free boundary) and precise asymptotic structure as Λ → ∞, refining the understanding of large-parameter Bernoulli problems.

title: Partition of unity a posteriori error estimators for the linear elasticity eigenvalue problem
summary: In this paper we consider the linear elasticity eigenvalue problem with different boundary conditions and examine two a posteriori error estimators, that compute solutions to local residual problems using a partition of unity and localized residuals. These a posteriori error estimators are known for the source problem, and in this paper we investigate their reliability and efficiency for the given eigenvalue problem with Dirichlet, Neumann and gliding boundary conditions. In numerical experiments we test the performance of the estimators on different domains, with different boundary conditions, and with different polynomial degrees. The numerical experiments show efficiency indices closer to one compared to the standard residual-based a posteriori error estimator.

AI.tldr: This paper studies two partition-of-unity based a posteriori error estimators for the linear elasticity eigenvalue problem under Dirichlet, Neumann, and gliding boundary conditions, proving reliability and efficiency and showing improved efficiency indices over standard residual-based estimators.
AI.motivation: A posteriori error estimators based on local residual problems with partition of unity and localized residuals are known for the source problem, but their reliability and efficiency for the linear elasticity eigenvalue problem across different boundary conditions had not been investigated.
AI.method: Two a posteriori error estimators are examined, which compute solutions to local residual problems using a partition of unity and localized residuals. Reliability and efficiency are analyzed for the eigenvalue problem with Dirichlet, Neumann, and gliding boundary conditions. Numerical experiments test the estimators on various domains, boundary conditions, and polynomial degrees.
AI.result: The numerical experiments show efficiency indices closer to one compared to the standard residual-based a posteriori error estimator.
AI.conclusion: The partition-of-unity based estimators are reliable and efficient for the linear elasticity eigenvalue problem and outperform the standard residual-based estimator in terms of efficiency indices.

title: Large-Time Behavior of Pseudo-Parabolic Equations Associated with Generalized Total Variation Energies
summary: In this paper, we study the well-posedness and large-time behavior of a pseudo-parabolic problem associated with a generalized total variation energy in the $BV$-framework. A main mathematical issue arises from the mismatch between the Sobolev regularity of solutions at finite times and the $BV$-structure of the corresponding steady-state problem. We prove the existence and uniqueness of solutions and investigate the relationship between their large-time behavior and solutions to the steady-state problem. Moreover, our results include the convergence of the solution trajectory to the unique steady-state solution under a typical setting arising in image processing.

AI.tldr: The paper establishes well-posedness and large-time behavior of a pseudo-parabolic problem governed by a generalized total variation energy in the BV framework, addressing the regularity mismatch between finite-time Sobolev solutions and the BV steady-state problem.
AI.motivation: A key mathematical difficulty stems from the mismatch between the Sobolev regularity of finite-time solutions and the BV-structure of the associated steady-state problem.
AI.method: Analysis within the BV-framework of a pseudo-parabolic problem tied to a generalized total variation energy, proving existence and uniqueness and relating large-time behavior to the steady-state problem.
AI.result: Existence and uniqueness of solutions are proven, and the relationship between large-time behavior and steady-state solutions is characterized, including convergence to the unique steady state in a typical image-processing setting.
AI.conclusion: The solution trajectory converges to the unique steady-state solution under a typical image-processing configuration.

title: A stabilized, nodal strain finite element method for small and large deformations: formulation, analysis, and impact on remeshing strategies
summary:
We present in this article the discretization of small and finite strain mechanics using
  variationally consistent, stabilized, nodal strain finite element formulations. We prove that
  these methods derive from a mixed variational principle that uses different meshes for the primal
  and dual variables. We demonstrate that, for both mechanical problems, nodal strain finite
  elements can be written as pure primal formulations with assumed strain operators. The
  stabilization terms are shown to be necessary and a new, general class of stabilizing functions is
  proposed for the finite strain regime. The ensuing formulations can be interpreted as pure
  particle methods because all kinematic and material information is stored at the nodes. This point
  of view explains the favorable properties of nodal strain methods when employed in problems that
  require frequent remeshing and involve inelastic materials. In these cases, the diffusion of
  internal variables is kept to a minimum. The numerical examples presented validate the claims.

AI.tldr: The paper develops stabilized nodal strain finite element formulations for small and finite strain mechanics, proving they arise from a mixed variational principle and can be recast as pure primal formulations with a new class of stabilizing functions.
AI.motivation: Nodal strain methods perform well in problems requiring frequent remeshing and involving inelastic materials, but a rigorous variational foundation and a general stabilization framework—especially for the finite strain regime—were lacking.
AI.method: Discretize small and finite strain mechanics using variationally consistent, stabilized nodal strain FE formulations. Prove they derive from a mixed variational principle using different meshes for primal and dual variables, rewrite them as pure primal formulations with assumed strain operators, and propose a new general class of stabilizing functions for finite strain.
AI.result: Stabilization terms are shown to be necessary, and the resulting formulations can be interpreted as pure particle methods since all kinematic and material information is stored at the nodes. Numerical examples validate the claims.
AI.conclusion: The nodal (particle) viewpoint explains the favorable properties of nodal strain methods, notably minimal diffusion of internal variables in remeshing and inelastic problems.

title: Low Mach number limit of the compressible Euler--Vlasov--Fokker--Planck system in the whole space
summary: Although there are many important contributions on compressible and incompressible fluid-particle interaction models respectively, how to connect the two-type fluid-particle models via the low Mach number limit remains a challenging open problem. In this paper, we resolve it for the compressible isentropic fluid-particle model (Euler--Vlasov--Fokker--Planck (Euler--VFP) system) in the whole space $\mathbb{R}^3$. First, we establish the global-in-time {\it a priori estimates} of strong solutions that are uniform with respect to the Mach number $\varepsilon$ near the global Maxwellian. The proof relies on a refined energy method that combines the relaxation structure $b^\varepsilon-u^\varepsilon$ induced by the fluid-particle interaction and the symmetrized acoustic structure of the compressible Euler part in the model. Under the assumption of well-prepared initial data, we derive a {\it global-in-time} uniform error estimate in the $H^2$ framework between the solution of the compressible Euler--VFP system and that of the limiting incompressible Euler--VFP system. A key point is to introduce the corrected acoustic variable $ q^\varepsilon-\varepsilon [P'(1)]^{-1}π$, which captures the pressure corrector in the low Mach number limit. This also allows us to exploit the exact cancellation of the singular acoustic terms and to close the {\it global-in-time} error estimate. The damping term $b^\varepsilon-u^\varepsilon$, which is absent in the pure Euler equations, plays an essential role in recovering the relative velocity dissipation and in controlling the coupled fluid-particle dynamics. As a consequence, we prove the low Mach number limit of the compressible Euler--VFP system with the convergence rate $\mathcal O(\varepsilon)$ in the time-continuous $H^2$ topology.

AI.tldr: This paper resolves the low Mach number limit connecting compressible and incompressible fluid-particle interaction models, proving a global-in-time convergence of the compressible Euler--Vlasov--Fokker--Planck system to its incompressible counterpart with rate O(ε) in H².
AI.motivation: Compressible and incompressible fluid-particle interaction models have been studied separately with major contributions, but connecting them via the low Mach number limit remained a challenging open problem.
AI.method: The authors establish global-in-time a priori estimates uniform in the Mach number ε near the global Maxwellian, using a refined energy method combining the relaxation structure b^ε − u^ε from fluid-particle interaction and the symmetrized acoustic structure of the compressible Euler part. They introduce a corrected acoustic variable q^ε − ε[P'(1)]⁻¹π to capture the pressure corrector and exploit exact cancellation of singular acoustic terms.
AI.result: Under well-prepared initial data, they derive a global-in-time uniform H² error estimate between the compressible and limiting incompressible Euler--VFP solutions, and prove the low Mach number limit with convergence rate O(ε) in time-continuous H² topology.
AI.conclusion: The low Mach number limit of the compressible Euler--VFP system is rigorously established, with the damping term b^ε − u^ε playing an essential role in recovering relative velocity dissipation and controlling coupled fluid-particle dynamics.

title: Structure-preserving quasi-interpolation for vector-valued function with multiple physical constraints
summary: We develop a unified theory of vectorial quasi-interpolation that exactly preserves intrinsic physical structures characterized by systems of linear constant-coefficient differential operators, including divergence-free and curl-free constraints as special cases. The key ingredient is a family of matrix-valued kernels constructed from an orthogonal projector in the frequency domain, whose columns analytically satisfy the prescribed constraints. The resulting quasi-interpolant is a weighted combination of kernel translates with sampled function values as coefficients, and therefore requires no constrained optimization. Simultaneous error estimates for the approximand and its derivatives are established within a bias-variance framework. For numerical vector-field decomposition, we introduce a generalized Helmholtz--Hodge decomposition that splits a smooth vector field into two components with distinct physical structures, and develop corresponding structure-preserving quasi-interpolation schemes and error estimates. Explicit kernels are derived for several representative constraints, including steady-state acoustic constraints, combined divergence-curl constraints, coupled divergence-free constraints, and second-order Saint-Venant compatibility conditions. Numerical experiments confirm the theoretical error estimates and exact structure preservation, demonstrate accurate identification of sources and sinks, and show three-dimensional reconstruction of generalized Helmholtz--Hodge components for general smooth vector fields without prior constraint assumptions.

AI.tldr: A unified vectorial quasi-interpolation theory preserves linear constant-coefficient differential operator structures (divergence-free, curl-free, etc.) using frequency-domain projector-based matrix kernels, requiring no constrained optimization.
AI.motivation: Existing methods for structure-preserving approximation often require constrained optimization and lack a unified treatment of general linear constant-coefficient differential constraints. A single framework is needed to exactly preserve intrinsic physical structures like divergence-free and curl-free conditions.
AI.method: Constructs a family of matrix-valued kernels from an orthogonal projector in the frequency domain whose columns analytically satisfy the prescribed constraints. The quasi-interpolant is a weighted combination of kernel translates with sampled values as coefficients, avoiding constrained optimization. Includes a bias-variance error analysis for the approximand and derivatives, and a generalized Helmholtz-Hodge decomposition with structure-preserving quasi-interpolation schemes.
AI.result: Simultaneous error estimates for the function and derivatives are established. Explicit kernels are derived for steady-state acoustic constraints, combined divergence-curl constraints, coupled divergence-free constraints, and second-order Saint-Venant compatibility. Numerical experiments confirm the error estimates, exact structure preservation, accurate source/sink identification, and 3D reconstruction of generalized Helmholtz-Hodge components without prior constraint assumptions.
AI.conclusion: The proposed unified quasi-interpolation framework exactly and efficiently preserves general linear constant-coefficient differential structures, providing a practical tool for vector-field decomposition and reconstruction.

title: Solving Large-Scale Sparse Linear Complementarity Problems Using a Shifted-Splitting Multi-Parameter Modulus-Based Iteration Method
summary: A shifted-splitting multi-parameter modulus-based iteration method is proposed for solving large sparse linear complementarity problems. The method introduces two additional parameters through a shifted matrix splitting while preserving the original coefficient matrix. Suitable choices of the splitting matrices generate Jacobi, Gauss-Seidel, SOR, and AOR-type schemes; the Gauss-Seidel type form is considered in the numerical experiments. Sufficient convergence results are established for $P$-matrices and $H_+$-matrices by using the spectral radius of the associated iteration matrix. For structured sparse matrices, sufficient parameter intervals ensuring the convergence of the proposed method are derived. An algorithm based on grid search is also developed to select efficient near-optimal parameter pairs for the numerical implementation. The influence of different parameter-matrix choices is examined through a sensitivity analysis. Numerical experiments on standard large sparse test problems demonstrate the efficiency of the proposed method compared with the tested projected-type method, the new modulus-based matrix splitting method, and the modulus-based matrix double splitting method in terms of iteration count, residual, and CPU time.

AI.tldr: A shifted-splitting multi-parameter modulus-based iteration method is proposed for large sparse linear complementarity problems, with convergence theory and a grid-search parameter selection algorithm.
AI.motivation: Solving large sparse linear complementarity problems efficiently requires methods that are both convergent and practically tunable; existing modulus-based schemes could benefit from additional flexibility via parameters and matrix splitting choices.
AI.method: The method introduces two extra parameters through a shifted matrix splitting while preserving the original coefficient matrix. Specific splitting matrix choices yield Jacobi, Gauss-Seidel, SOR, and AOR-type schemes (Gauss-Seidel form used in experiments). Convergence is proven for P-matrices and H_+-matrices via spectral radius of the iteration matrix, with parameter intervals derived for structured sparse matrices. A grid-search algorithm selects near-optimal parameter pairs, and sensitivity analysis examines parameter-matrix choices.
AI.result: Numerical experiments on standard large sparse test problems show the method outperforms a projected-type method, a new modulus-based matrix splitting method, and a modulus-based matrix double splitting method in iteration count, residual, and CPU time.
AI.conclusion: The proposed shifted-splitting multi-parameter modulus-based method is efficient and flexible for large sparse LCPs, with theoretical convergence guarantees and practical parameter selection.

title: Lyapunov Functions and $R$-Linear Convergence for Quadratic Barzilai-Borwein Dynamics
summary:
The Barzilai--Borwein (BB) method is $R$-linearly convergent on strongly convex quadratics, although neither the objective value nor the gradient norm is generally monotone. We construct an explicit current-point Lyapunov function for the quadratic dynamics after the warm-up step, assuming that both endpoints of the initial active spectrum survive this step. If $a<b$ are these endpoints and $P_a,P_b$ are the corresponding spectral projectors, then \[
  \overline{f}(x)
  :=\lVert P_a\nabla f(x)\rVert^{\frac{2b}{a+b}}
  \lVert P_b\nabla f(x)\rVert^{\frac{2a}{a+b}} \] satisfies, for BB1, BB2, and every fixed positive weighted delayed Rayleigh rule, \[
  \overline{f}(x_{k+1})
  =\left(\frac{b-a}{b+a}\right)^2
  e^{-2D_{a,b}(τ_k)}\overline{f}(x_k),
  \qquad D_{a,b}(τ_k)\ge0, \] where $τ_k=1/α_k$ is the reciprocal step. The function is obtained by denormalizing the endpoint coboundary certificate in the sharp-rate analysis of Yang and Yuan. We prove that the endpoint exponents are the unique minimax choice among endpoint monomials and illustrate the Lyapunov law on a nonmonotone BB1 trajectory. Using this law, we also give a proof of $R$-linear convergence of the method in finite dimensions.

AI.tldr: A Lyapunov function is constructed for the Barzilai--Borwein (BB) method on strongly convex quadratics, yielding a sharp oscillation law and a new proof of R-linear convergence.
AI.motivation: BB method converges R-linearly on strongly convex quadratics, but neither objective value nor gradient norm is monotone, so standard monotone descent arguments fail and a new certificate of convergence is needed.
AI.method: Constructs an explicit current-point Lyapunov function as a weighted product of endpoint spectral projector gradient norms, obtained by denormalizing the endpoint coboundary certificate of Yang--Yuan; proves endpoint exponents are the unique minimax choice among endpoint monomials.
AI.result: The Lyapunov function satisfies a sharp contraction law with factor ((b-a)/(b+a))^2 e^{-2D} for BB1, BB2, and every fixed positive weighted delayed Rayleigh rule; the law is illustrated on a nonmonotone BB1 trajectory.
AI.conclusion: Provides a finite-dimensional proof of R-linear convergence for BB-type methods via the constructed Lyapunov law.

title: Classification of solutions to the Liouville equation with a nonlinear Robin boundary condition on the unit disk

AI.tldr: Studies a nonlinear elliptic BVP with exponential nonlinearity on the unit disk and Robin-type boundary condition, providing complete solution classification for 0<λ≤2 and a radial/nonradial dichotomy for 2<λ≤3 via a new Hardy-Wronskian boundary rigidity method.
AI.motivation: The paper aims to classify smooth solutions of a Liouville-type boundary value problem with a Robin (nonlinear Neumann) boundary condition, understanding how the boundary parameter λ governs the solution structure.
AI.method: Develops a Hardy-Wronskian boundary rigidity method that converts the nonlinear BVP into a spectral rigidity problem for normalized holomorphic frames, exploiting the complex-analytic structure of the Liouville equation with a Robin boundary condition.
AI.result: For 0<λ≤2, a complete classification of smooth solutions is established. For 2<λ≤3, a dichotomy between radial and nonradial solutions is proved.
AI.conclusion: The method yields a new rigidity framework applicable to related two-dimensional elliptic boundary value problems and clarifies the solution structure across regimes of λ.

title: Global and Unconditional $R$-Linear Convergence of Rank-Compressed Weighted LMSD Sweeps for Strictly Convex Quadratics
summary: We study limited memory steepest descent (LMSD) with exact algebraic rank compression for strictly convex quadratic optimization. At each cycle, the method restricts the gradient history to its column space and applies the reciprocals of all Ritz values of the compressed projection in the next sweep. If the block-start gradient has at most $p$ active distinct eigenvalues, the delayed sweep terminates finitely. For nonterminating trajectories, a determinant and Cauchy--Binet formula for the complete-sweep polynomial yields global convergence without a full-rank history or a run-wise normalized-conditioning bound. Consecutive sweep endpoints define a continuous positively homogeneous map on a closed cone of compatible states. Compactness then gives an $R$-linear endpoint estimate, uniform over compatible initial states, with constants depending only on $H$ and $p$; the estimate extends to inner gradients, iterate errors, and objective gaps. Every fixed positive spectral weight $W=ω(H)$ is linearly conjugate to the standard method. The weighted methods therefore share its decay factor, while the Euclidean-norm prefactor is increased by at most $\sqrt{κ_2(W)}$. This includes harmonic-Ritz LMSD, fixed power weights, and the delayed BB1 and BB2 recurrences.

AI.tldr: The paper develops a theory of limited memory steepest descent (LMSD) with exact algebraic rank compression for strictly convex quadratic minimization, establishing finite termination and global R-linear convergence without full-rank history assumptions.
AI.motivation: Existing LMSD analyses often require a full-rank history or run-wise normalized-conditioning bounds, which limit their applicability. The authors seek a sharper convergence theory that avoids these assumptions.
AI.method: They restrict the gradient history to its column space (exact algebraic rank compression) and apply reciprocals of all Ritz values of the compressed projection in the next sweep. They analyze complete-sweep polynomials via determinant and Cauchy--Binet formulas, and model consecutive sweep endpoints as a continuous positively homogeneous map on a closed cone of compatible states.
AI.result: If the block-start gradient has at most p active distinct eigenvalues, the delayed sweep terminates finitely. For nonterminating trajectories, global convergence holds without a full-rank history or run-wise normalized-conditioning bound. Compactness yields an R-linear endpoint estimate uniform over compatible initial states, with constants depending only on H and p, extending to inner gradients, iterate errors, and objective gaps. Weighted methods share the standard decay factor, with Euclidean-norm prefactor increased by at most sqrt(kappa_2(W)).
AI.conclusion: Limited memory steepest descent with exact algebraic rank compression admits finite termination and uniform global R-linear convergence. All fixed positive spectral weights are linearly conjugate to the standard method, covering harmonic-Ritz LMSD, fixed power weights, and delayed BB1/BB2 recurrences.

title: Non-radial minimizers for the first eigenvalue of the Laplacian in cones and a related overdetermined problem
comment: 38 pages. All comments are much welcome
summary: In this work, we consider relative overdetermined problems for the first eigenfunction of the Laplacian for domains in cones, and the related question of minimizing the first eigenvalue among sets of a given fixed measure. By means of a shape derivative analysis, we show that the spherical sector is a critical shape and obtain a geometric condition on the cone for its stability/instability. By a concentration-compactness argument, we prove the existence of a minimizer, which moreover is bounded, open, connected, and whose relative boundary is regular almost everywhere. By another domain variation argument, we conclude that the minimizers admit a solution for the overdetermined problem.

AI.tldr: This paper studies relative overdetermined problems for the first Laplacian eigenfunction in conical domains and the minimization of the first eigenvalue under fixed measure, proving existence and regularity of minimizers and characterizing the spherical sector's stability.
AI.motivation: The authors aim to extend overdetermined eigenvalue problems, typically posed on bounded domains, to domains inside cones, where the geometry of the cone boundary interacts with the overdetermined condition, motivating the question of how the first eigenvalue behaves under domain variation.
AI.method: The approach combines a shape derivative analysis to identify the spherical sector as a critical shape and derive a geometric stability/instability condition on the cone, with a concentration-compactness argument to establish existence of a minimizer. A further domain variation argument links minimizers to solutions of the overdetermined problem.
AI.result: The spherical sector is shown to be a critical shape, with stability or instability governed by a geometric condition on the cone. A minimizer of the first eigenvalue at fixed measure is proven to exist and is bounded, open, connected, with relative boundary regular almost everywhere. Minimizers admit a solution to the overdetermined problem.
AI.conclusion: The work establishes existence, geometric structure, and regularity of minimizers for the first eigenvalue in cones, and connects them to relative overdetermined eigenvalue problems via domain variation, while characterizing stability of the spherical sector through the cone's geometry.

title: Grid-Free Monte Carlo for Time-Dependent Diffusion
summary: Many scientific applications require modeling how diffusive systems evolve over time, not merely their eventual steady states. While conventional steady-state analysis of partial differential equations (PDEs) on complex geometries is already hindered by costly volumetric meshing, transient analysis further requires sequential time stepping and careful step size selection. Grid-free Monte Carlo solvers such as walk on spheres (WoS) and walk on stars (WoSt) avoid this meshing bottleneck but remain largely limited to steady-state problems. We generalize WoS, for pure Dirichlet problems, and WoSt, for mixed Dirichlet--Neumann problems, to heat equations with initial conditions and time-dependent source and boundary data. We equip each random walk with a finite time budget and sample an exit time at every spatial step. If the exit time exceeds the remaining budget, the walk samples an interior point and evaluates the initial condition; otherwise, it continues with a reduced budget, accumulating source and boundary contributions. Our main technical contribution is a suite of kernel sampling and variance reduction techniques, including a low-bias, tabulation-free exit time sampler and efficient rejection samplers. Unlike grid-based transient solvers, our method directly estimates the solution at any requested time without volumetric meshing or sequential time marching. It also retains the parallel, progressive, and output-sensitive evaluation of WoS and WoSt while eliminating time step selection and temporal discretization bias entirely. Finally, we show how sharing walks enables efficient estimates at multiple target times.

AI.tldr: This paper generalizes grid-free Monte Carlo solvers (Walk on Spheres/Stars) from steady-state to transient heat equations by equipping walks with a finite time budget and sampling exit times, enabling direct estimation at any time without meshing or time stepping.
AI.motivation: Steady-state PDE analysis on complex geometries is hindered by costly volumetric meshing, and transient analysis additionally requires sequential time stepping with careful step-size selection. Existing grid-free Monte Carlo solvers avoid meshing but are largely limited to steady-state problems.
AI.method: Extends WoS (pure Dirichlet) and WoSt (mixed Dirichlet-Neumann) to heat equations with initial conditions and time-dependent source/boundary data. Each random walk carries a finite time budget and samples an exit time at every spatial step: if the exit time exceeds the remaining budget, it samples an interior point and evaluates the initial condition; otherwise it continues with a reduced budget while accumulating source and boundary contributions. Key contributions include kernel sampling and variance reduction techniques, a low-bias tabulation-free exit time sampler, and efficient rejection samplers.
AI.result: The method directly estimates the solution at any requested time without volumetric meshing or sequential time marching, eliminating time step selection and temporal discretization bias while retaining parallel, progressive, and output-sensitive evaluation. Sharing walks enables efficient estimates at multiple target times.
AI.conclusion: The proposed approach extends grid-free Monte Carlo PDE solving to transient heat equations, providing a meshing-free, step-free, and unbiased alternative to grid-based transient solvers.

title: On space-time derivative estimates for the magnetohydrodynamic equations
summary: In this paper, we present the space-time derivative estimates of solutions to the MHD equations. It is a generalization of a priori bounds for the classical Navier-Stokes system by Duff in \cite[Acta Math. 164, 1990]{[Duff]} and gives an affirmative answer to a question proposed by Zheligovsky in \cite[Mathematics. 9, 2021]{[Zheligovsky]}. In addition, we show that $u, B \in L^{\f{q}{q-3}}(0,T;L^{q} (\mathbb{R}^{3}))$ with $6\leq q\leq\infty $ and $ D ^{k}u, D ^{k}B \in L^{\f{q}{ q(k+1)-3}}(0,T;L^{q} (\mathbb{R}^{3}))$ for $k\geq1, 2\leq q\leq\infty$ in this system.

AI.tldr: The paper establishes space-time derivative estimates for solutions of the MHD equations, extending Duff's a priori bounds for the Navier-Stokes system and answering a question posed by Zheligovsky. It also derives new $L^q_t L^q_x$ regularity results for $u$, $B$ and their higher derivatives.
AI.motivation: Duff established a priori bounds for the classical Navier-Stokes system, and Zheligovsky posed a question about whether analogous estimates hold for the MHD equations. This paper aims to generalize those bounds to MHD and provide an affirmative answer.
AI.method: The authors develop space-time derivative estimates for solutions to the MHD equations, generalizing the a priori bound techniques used by Duff for the Navier-Stokes system.
AI.result: The paper proves that $u, B \in L^{q/(q-3)}(0,T;L^{q}(\mathbb{R}^3))$ for $6 \leq q \leq \infty$, and $D^k u, D^k B \in L^{q/(q(k+1)-3)}(0,T;L^{q}(\mathbb{R}^3))$ for $k \geq 1$, $2 \leq q \leq \infty$.
AI.conclusion: The space-time derivative estimates for MHD solutions generalize Duff's Navier-Stokes bounds and affirmatively answer Zheligovsky's question, with additional $L^q_t L^q_x$ regularity results for the velocity and magnetic fields and their derivatives.

title: Inference for Newton Methods with Accelerated Sketch-and-Project via Random Scaling
summary: We study an online sketched Newton method that approximates the Newton direction at each step via a state-of-the-art sketching solver, called the generalized accelerated sketch-and-project solver (GAS), thereby mitigating the computational bottleneck of classical second-order methods. The GAS solver improves upon vanilla, unaccelerated sketch-and-project solvers by achieving accelerated convergence through Nesterov momentum updates, and accommodates a flexible projection metric whose proper choice further reduces computational cost. Building on this design, we establish asymptotic normality of the averaged sketched Newton iterates and characterize their limiting covariance matrix. The resulting covariance recovers that of the unaccelerated sketched Newton method under a specific choice of acceleration parameters, converges more rapidly (in the number of sketching steps) to the minimax-optimal covariance in general, and is smaller than that of the last iterate produced by the accelerated method. Finally, we strengthen these results by establishing a functional central limit theorem for the Newton iterates, which allows us to bypass explicit covariance estimation and develop an online inference procedure based on random scaling. Specifically, we construct a pivotal test statistic by appropriately rescaling the averaged iterates, so that its limiting distribution is free of any unknown parameters, enabling asymptotically valid online inference. Numerical experiments demonstrate superior performance of the proposed inference procedure.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes an online sketched Newton method using the Generalized Accelerated Sketch-and-project (GAS) solver, establishing asymptotic normality of averaged iterates and developing an online inference procedure via a functional central limit theorem.
AI.motivation: Classical second-order (Newton) methods suffer from a computational bottleneck, and vanilla sketch-and-project solvers lack acceleration. There is a need for a faster sketched Newton method with rigorous statistical guarantees to enable efficient online inference.
AI.method: The method approximates the Newton direction at each step via the GAS solver, which uses Nesterov momentum updates and a flexible projection metric. The authors establish asymptotic normality of averaged sketched Newton iterates, characterize the limiting covariance matrix, and prove a functional central limit theorem for the iterates.
AI.result: The limiting covariance recovers that of the unaccelerated method under specific acceleration parameters, converges faster to the minimax-optimal covariance, and is smaller than that of the accelerated method's last iterate. A pivotal test statistic is constructed via random scaling, yielding a limiting distribution free of unknown parameters for asymptotically valid online inference. Numerical experiments show superior performance.
AI.conclusion: The GAS-based sketched Newton method offers accelerated convergence and enables parameter-free online inference through random scaling, providing both theoretical guarantees and practical superiority over existing approaches.

title: Weak Solutions for the Unregularised Hibler Momentum Equation with Degenerate Coefficients
summary: We study the momentum equation of the decoupled unregularised Hibler sea-ice model with non-negative ice mass and ice strength, both of which may vanish. The ocean drag provides coercivity, while the stress law and mixed boundary conditions are encoded by a convex dissipation functional. We prove existence, uniqueness and stability for the time-discrete problem and reconstruct an admissible stress. A Rothe approximation yields global weak variational solutions for time-dependent coefficients under a one-sided growth condition on the mass. Weak solutions are unique when the ice strength is independent of time. For spatially Lipschitz ice strength, finite dissipation also yields a local measure structure of the weighted deformation and a global bound on the negative part of the weighted divergence.

AI.tldr: The paper analyzes the momentum equation of the decoupled, unregularised Hibler sea-ice model, allowing ice mass and strength to be non-negative and possibly vanishing. It proves existence, uniqueness, and stability for the time-discrete problem, reconstructs an admissible stress, and via a Rothe approximation establishes global weak variational solutions with a one-sided growth condition on mass.
AI.motivation: Sea-ice models like Hibler's are typically regularized to avoid degeneracies when ice mass or strength vanish. This work addresses the unregularised, coupled physical setting, seeking to handle vanishing ice mass and strength while retaining the ocean drag's coercivity and the stress law's convex dissipation structure.
AI.method: Uses a convex dissipation functional to encode the stress law and mixed boundary conditions. Proves time-discrete well-posedness and stress reconstruction, then applies a Rothe (time-discretization) approximation to obtain global weak variational solutions under a one-sided growth condition on the mass.
AI.result: Establishes existence, uniqueness, and stability for the time-discrete problem; global weak variational solutions for time-dependent coefficients under one-sided mass growth. Solutions are unique when ice strength is time-independent. For spatially Lipschitz ice strength, finite dissipation yields local measure structure of weighted deformation and a global bound on the negative part of weighted divergence.
AI.conclusion: The unregularised Hibler momentum model admits global weak solutions despite degeneracies, with uniqueness under time-independent ice strength and refined regularity (measure-valued deformation, divergence bounds) for Lipschitz strength.

title: Controlling the energy jump of multistable structures using shape optimization
summary: Multistable systems admit distinct stable equilibria for the same loading and boundary conditions. Shape optimization of multistable structures offers a promising route to engineer the mechanical response of advanced materials and metamaterials. In this work, we develop a formulation and algorithm for controlling the energy jump associated with snap-through behaviour in hyperelastic metamaterials by optimizing the shape of the domain. The key challenge is that classical shape optimization theory assumes a single-valued domain-to-solution map, which does not hold in the multistable setting. We address this by extending the theory to settings with non-unique solutions, treating the scaling of the domain deformation as a continuation parameter and applying the implicit function theorem to give sufficient conditions for the continued existence of multiple solution branches as the shape varies. This theoretical foundation underpins a practical algorithm that targets a prescribed energy jump between stable states, enabling the systematic design of structures whose snap-through response can be tuned on demand.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a shape optimization formulation and algorithm for controlling the energy jump in snap-through of hyperelastic multistable metamaterials by extending classical shape optimization theory to non-unique solution settings.
AI.motivation: Multistable systems have distinct stable equilibria under the same loading/boundary conditions, enabling tunable mechanical responses. Shape optimization could engineer these responses, but classical shape optimization theory assumes a single-valued domain-to-solution map, which fails for multistable structures.
AI.method: The theory is extended to non-unique solutions: the scaling of the domain deformation is treated as a continuation parameter, and the implicit function theorem provides sufficient conditions for continued existence of multiple solution branches as the shape varies. This underpins a practical algorithm targeting a prescribed energy jump between stable states.
AI.result: A practical algorithm that targets a prescribed energy jump between stable states, enabling systematic design of structures with on-demand tunable snap-through response.
AI.conclusion: The extended shape optimization framework enables systematic design of hyperelastic metamaterials whose snap-through energy jump can be tuned on demand.

title: Regularity of Structurally Stable Cusp Singularities for Two Families of Quasilinear Wave-type Equations
summary: In this paper, we study two families of quasilinear equations: Hunter-Saxton type and Camassa-Hom type equations, with a paramerter $λ\in(0,1)$ whose solutions form cusp singularities. When $λ=1$, the first system becomes the scalar conservation law. The main result of this paper is to give regularity of two types of structurally stable singularities: Type I on the singular curve, Type II at the point where cusp singularity forms, for some $λ\in(0,1)$. When $λ\rightarrow 1$, our result indicts the $C^{1/3}$ regularity at the point where singularity forms, which agrees with the regularity of the generic pre-shock solution.

AI.tldr: This paper studies Hunter-Saxton and Camassa-Holm type quasilinear equations with parameter λ∈(0,1) whose solutions form cusp singularities, establishing regularity of two structurally stable singularity types.
AI.motivation: Understanding how cusp singularities form and their regularity in quasilinear equations like Hunter-Saxton and Camassa-Holm types, and connecting to the scalar conservation law limit (λ=1) and pre-shock solutions.
AI.method: Analyze two families of quasilinear equations (Hunter-Saxton type and Camassa-Holm type) with parameter λ∈(0,1); study two structurally stable singularity types—Type I on the singular curve and Type II at the point where cusp singularity forms.
AI.result: Establishes regularity of Type I and Type II structurally stable singularities for some λ∈(0,1); as λ→1, obtains C^{1/3} regularity at the point where the singularity forms.
AI.conclusion: The C^{1/3} regularity in the λ→1 limit agrees with the regularity of the generic pre-shock solution, linking the cusp singularity formation to known conservation-law behavior.

title: Quantile-based Loss Filtering for Outlier-Robust Stochastic Gradient Descent
summary: We study loss-based filtering for finite-sum optimization with a subset of corrupted component functions whose gradients may be highly unreliable. Motivated by minimum-loss-based SGD (min-$k$-loss) and quantile-based methods for corrupted linear systems, we propose and analyze a general loss-filtering framework -- Quantile-\(k\)-Loss SGD (Q\(k\)L-SGD) -- that samples \(k\) component losses at each iteration and updates using an index chosen uniformly from the lower empirical \(q\)-quantile. We prove linear convergence of this family of methods under standard convexity assumptions, requiring the sample size to scale with the number of corruptions and a subset strong-convexity threshold. For the cases when large enough sampling is impossible or undesirable, we give a complementary small-sample probabilistic analysis that covers any sample size $k$ and the convergence behavior depends on the probability of selecting an outlier and on the curvature of the selected good step. Experiments on polynomial regression, regularized logistic regression, and regularized hinge loss show that intermediate quantiles often outperform both standard SGD and min-\(k\)-loss SGD. In particular, min-\(k\) often stalls by repeatedly selecting nearly solved components, while intermediate quantiles retain robustness and produce more informative updates.

AI.tldr: Proposes Quantile-k-Loss SGD (QkL-SGD), a loss-filtering framework for finite-sum optimization with corrupted components, with linear convergence guarantees and complementary small-sample analysis.
AI.motivation: Gradients from a subset of corrupted component functions are highly unreliable, and standard SGD or min-k-loss SGD can fail or stall. A more general loss-filtering approach is needed to balance robustness and informative updates.
AI.method: QkL-SGD samples k component losses per iteration and updates using an index chosen uniformly from the lower empirical q-quantile. The authors prove linear convergence under convexity, requiring sample size to scale with corruption count and a subset strong-convexity threshold. A small-sample probabilistic analysis covers any k, with behavior depending on outlier-selection probability and curvature of the good step.
AI.result: Linear convergence is established for the general framework; small-sample analysis characterizes convergence for arbitrary k. Experiments on polynomial regression, regularized logistic regression, and regularized hinge loss show intermediate quantiles often outperform standard SGD and min-k-loss SGD, while min-k often stalls by repeatedly selecting nearly solved components.
AI.conclusion: QkL-SGD provides a flexible, robust filtering framework for corrupted finite-sum optimization, with intermediate quantiles offering better robustness and more informative updates than standard or min-k-loss baselines.

title: Perturbative Schauder Estimates for $Q$-Valued Quasilinear Elliptic Systems and a Sharp Dimension Bound for Branch Sets of Stationary Graphs
summary: We establish a priori interior $C^{1,α}$ and $C^{2,α}$ Schauder estimates for a class of $Q$-valued quasilinear elliptic systems which are perturbations of the Laplace system, for arbitrary multiplicity $Q$, domain dimension $n\geq2$, and target dimension $k$. The $C^{1,α}$ estimate generalises the work of Simon and Wickramasekera in \cite{SW16} on $2$-valued solutions of linear systems and concerns weak solutions of divergence-form systems, while the $C^{2,α}$ estimate concerns strong solutions. In dimension $n=2$, both estimates hold for every $0<α<1/Q$. In dimensions $n\geq3$, there exists $δ=δ(n,k,Q)>0$ such that both estimates hold for every $0<α<δ$. As applications, we obtain a small-slope Schauder estimate and a small-slope Bernstein theorem for $Q$-valued maps whose graph varifolds are stationary. Combining the Schauder estimate with the recent branch-set stratification theory of Krummel--Minter--Wickramasekera in \cite{KMW26}, we further prove that, for every $γ>0$, the branch set $\mathcal B_u$ of any $C^{1,γ}$ $Q$-valued map $u$ whose graph varifold is stationary satisfies $\dim_{\mathcal H}\mathcal B_u\leq n-2$. This bound is sharp already in codimension one.

AI.tldr: The paper proves interior C^{1,α} and C^{2,α} Schauder estimates for Q-valued quasilinear elliptic systems perturbing the Laplace system, for any Q, n≥2, k, plus applications to small-slope estimates, a Bernstein theorem, and a sharp branch-set dimension bound.
AI.motivation: Extend Schauder theory from 2-valued linear systems (Simon–Wickramasekera) to general Q-valued quasilinear elliptic systems, providing regularity tools for stationary Q-valued maps and their branch sets.
AI.method: Establish a priori interior C^{1,α} (weak, divergence-form) and C^{2,α} (strong) Schauder estimates; ranges α<1/Q in n=2 and α<δ(n,k,Q) in n≥3; combine with Krummel–Minter–Wickramasekera branch-set stratification.
AI.result: Schauder estimates hold for all 0<α<1/Q when n=2, and for 0<α<δ(n,k,Q) when n≥3. Applications: small-slope Schauder estimate, small-slope Bernstein theorem for stationary graph varifolds, and dim_H B_u ≤ n−2 for C^{1,γ} Q-valued maps with stationary graph varifold, sharp in codimension one.
AI.conclusion: The results generalize prior 2-valued linear Schauder theory to Q-valued quasilinear systems and yield optimal branch-set dimension bounds via stratification theory.

title: Fractional porous medium equation on manifolds with nonnegative Ricci curvature: existence of solutions and smoothing effects via potential methods
summary: We study the fractional porous medium equation on complete noncompact Riemannian manifolds with nonnegative Ricci curvature for $s\in(0,1]$ and $n>2s$. Assuming that the manifold is $s$-nonparabolic, so that the fractional Laplacian admits a suitable positive minimal Green function, we use this Green function to introduce a natural weighted space of initial data, strictly larger than $L^1$. This leads to a weak dual, or potential, formulation of the equation, for which we prove existence for nonnegative initial data in the weighted space. We then establish quantitative local smoothing estimates for initial data in either $L^1$ or the Green-weighted space. Under additional noncollapsing and uniform volume-growth assumptions, we obtain global smoothing estimates. We also show that, even in $\mathbb{R}^n$, data in the Green-weighted space need not generate bounded solutions unless a suitable uniform weighted integrability condition is imposed. The short- and long-time behaviors predicted by our estimates are shown to be optimal in appropriate senses. When $s\in(0,1/2)$, the results require only $\operatorname{Ric}\geq0$, together with a noncollapsing assumption where needed. Our estimates also cover the case $s=1$, several of them being new in that setting. Finally, we extend the approach to more general filtration equations.
