AI.tldr: The paper develops a potential (weak dual) formulation of the fractional porous medium equation on complete noncompact manifolds with nonnegative Ricci curvature, using the minimal Green function to define a weighted data space larger than L^1, and proves optimal local/global smoothing estimates.
AI.motivation: The fractional porous medium equation on curved, noncompact manifolds lacks a natural framework for initial data beyond L^1, since the fractional Laplacian's Green function permits a broader class of admissible data. The authors seek a formulation that captures this larger class and yields sharp smoothing behavior.
AI.method: Assuming s-nonparabolicity (s in (0,1], n > 2s), they use the positive minimal Green function of the fractional Laplacian to define a weighted space of initial data strictly larger than L^1, and introduce a weak dual/potential formulation. They prove existence for nonnegative data and derive quantitative local smoothing estimates; under noncollapsing and uniform volume-growth assumptions they obtain global smoothing. Counterexamples in R^n show the necessity of a uniform weighted integrability condition.
AI.result: Existence for nonnegative initial data in the Green-weighted space; quantitative local smoothing estimates for data in L^1 or the weighted space; global smoothing estimates under noncollapsing and volume-growth conditions; optimality of short- and long-time behavior; for s in (0,1/2) only Ric >= 0 is needed; results also new for s = 1. Data in the weighted space need not yield bounded solutions without a uniform weighted integrability condition, even in R^n.
AI.conclusion: The Green-function-based potential formulation provides a natural and sharp setting for the fractional porous medium equation on nonnegatively curved manifolds, with optimal smoothing estimates, and extends to more general filtration equations.

title: Differential Harnack inequalities and maximum principles of Morel-Oswald type for elliptic PDE in divergence form
comment: This preprint stems from preprint ArXiV 2411.19367, which was split in two parts, and whose results have been substantially improved and extended
summary: This paper presents two types of novel, qualitative and quantitative, estimates for positive solutions of general uniformly elliptic PDEs in divergence form. First, we prove a Morel-Oswald type of extension of the Hopf-Oleinik lemma, in which in addition we specify the sharp dependence of the constant in the data of the operator and the size of the domain. Second, we establish a new differential Harnack (logarithmic gradient) estimate for non-homogeneous equations, as well as an optimal global differential Harnack estimate for homogeneous equations.

AI.tldr: The paper establishes qualitative and quantitative estimates for positive solutions of uniformly elliptic PDEs in divergence form, including a Morel-Oswald-type Hopf-Oleinik lemma with sharp constant dependence and new (optimal) differential Harnack estimates.
AI.motivation: Positive solutions of uniformly elliptic divergence-form PDEs are central to the theory of elliptic equations, and the well-known Hopf-Oleinik lemma and Harnack estimates are key tools. Existing versions often lack sharp quantitative dependence on the operator data and domain size, and differential Harnack estimates for non-homogeneous equations remain limited.
AI.method: The authors prove two types of estimates. First, they obtain a Morel-Oswald type extension of the Hopf-Oleinik lemma, in which the sharp dependence of the constant on the operator data and the domain size is specified. Second, they establish a new differential Harnack (logarithmic gradient) estimate for non-homogeneous equations, alongside an optimal global differential Harnack estimate for homogeneous equations.
AI.result: Qualitative and quantitative estimates are obtained: a sharp-dependent Hopf-Oleinik type boundary lemma (Morel-Oswald extension), a new differential Harnack estimate for non-homogeneous equations, and an optimal global differential Harnack estimate for homogeneous equations.
AI.conclusion: The work extends classical results for uniformly elliptic divergence-form PDEs, providing sharp quantitative control in the Hopf-Oleinik lemma and introducing (optimal) differential Harnack estimates, thereby enriching the analytic toolkit for positive solutions of such equations.

title: Stable determination of coefficients for the nonlinear third-order acoustic equations
summary: In this paper, we study an inverse boundary value problem for a generalized Jordan-Moore-Gibson-Thompson equation with Westervelt-type nonlinearity and space-dependent coefficients. This third-order (in time) hyperbolic equation models nonlinear ultrasound propagation in viscous and thermally relaxing media. Assuming that the diffusivity and the sound speed are known a priori, we investigate the simultaneous stable determination of the friction coefficient, the weak damping coefficient, the potential, and the nonlinear coefficient from the associated Dirichlet-to-Neumann map. The proof combines the finite-difference linearization method with the construction of Gaussian beam and geometric optics solutions. These arguments reduce the inverse problem to stability estimates for (attenuated) geodesic ray transforms under the foliation condition. As a consequence, we obtain Hölder-type stability estimates of recovering the linear and nonlinear coefficients.

AI.tldr: The paper studies inverse boundary value problem for a generalized Jordan-Moore-Gibson-Thompson equation with Westervelt nonlinearity, proving Hölder-type stability in recovering four coefficients from Dirichlet-to-Neumann map data.
AI.motivation: This third-order-in-time hyperbolic equation models nonlinear ultrasound propagation in viscous and thermally relaxing media, and there is a need to stably determine unknown medium parameters from boundary measurements.
AI.method: Assumes diffusivity and sound speed are known a priori; combines finite-difference linearization with Gaussian beam and geometric optics solutions, reducing the problem to stability estimates for attenuated geodesic ray transforms under the foliation condition.
AI.result: Obtains Hölder-type stability estimates for simultaneously recovering the friction coefficient, weak damping coefficient, potential, and nonlinear coefficient from the Dirichlet-to-Neumann map.
AI.conclusion: Stable simultaneous determination of both linear and nonlinear coefficients is achievable for this nonlinear ultrasound model under the stated geometric and a priori assumptions.

title: Dispersive decay and scattering for continuum Calogero--Moser models
summary: We prove pointwise decay and scattering for small-mass solutions to the focusing and defocusing continuum Calogero--Moser models under suitable decay assumptions on the initial data. Our proof is based on an explicit formula for solutions and the exact conservation of the Galilean vector field associated to the equation.

AI.tldr: Pointwise decay and scattering are proved for small-mass solutions of focusing and defocusing continuum Calogero–Moser models under suitable initial-data decay assumptions.
AI.motivation: Scattering and pointwise decay are fundamental long-time behaviors for dispersive PDEs, and the continuum Calogero–Moser model's asymptotic behavior in the small-mass regime was not previously established.
AI.method: Uses an explicit solution formula combined with exact conservation of the Galilean vector field associated to the equation.
AI.result: Establishes pointwise decay and scattering for small-mass solutions, for both focusing and defocusing variants, given suitable decay of initial data.
AI.conclusion: The explicit formula and Galilean invariance are key tools yielding decay and scattering in the small-mass continuum Calogero–Moser setting.

title: Dispersive estimates for the Landau Hamiltonian on the hyperbolic plane
summary: In this paper, We obtain dispersive estimates for solutions to the Schrödinger equation with a uniform magnetic field on the hyperbolic plane \(\mathbb{H}\). The key ingredient is an explicit representation formula for the kernel of the corresponding Schrödinger propagator. As a consequence, we prove the corresponding Strichartz estimates for all admissible pairs on \(\mathbb{H}\).

AI.tldr: Dispersive and Strichartz estimates are obtained for the Schrödinger equation with a uniform magnetic field on the hyperbolic plane.
AI.motivation: Strichartz and dispersive estimates are fundamental in harmonic analysis and PDE, but the magnetic Schrödinger setting on the hyperbolic plane lacks a systematic treatment. This paper fills that gap.
AI.method: The key tool is an explicit representation formula for the kernel of the Schrödinger propagator associated with the uniform magnetic field on the hyperbolic plane.
AI.result: Dispersive estimates for the solutions are established, and as a consequence, Strichartz estimates are proved for all admissible pairs on the hyperbolic plane.
AI.conclusion: The explicit propagator kernel enables a complete set of dispersive and Strichartz estimates for the magnetic Schrödinger equation on the hyperbolic plane.

title: Parity-Skeleton First-Passage Dynamics and Optimal Intervention in Two-Sided Discrete Monitoring Systems
summary: Two-sided threshold crossings arise in discrete monitoring systems whenever intervention is triggered by departure from an operating band. This paper develops a finite-state first-passage framework based on a biased random walk with symmetric absorbing barriers. To remove parity gaps of the raw hitting time, we analyse a parity-corrected lifetime through even- and odd-state Markov skeletons. Adjacent-row likelihood-ratio inequalities verify the monotonicity condition and establish increasing failure rate and new-better-than-used properties. These ageing properties yield log-concave survival probabilities and geometric persistence bounds. Substochastic-matrix formulas are derived for survival, hazard, mean lifetime, state-conditioned remaining useful life, and finite-horizon crossing risk. A renewal-cost criterion then converts the first-passage distribution into an optimal preventive-intervention schedule. Model parameters are obtained by matching the drift and variance of observed increments to a two-point random-walk approximation, with a rolling-window extension for nonstationary regimes. Numerical experiments compare exact calculations with Monte Carlo diagnostics, moment-matched inverse-Gaussian and Weibull benchmarks, serially correlated increments, calibration perturbations, and fixed-interval policies. A synthetic remote-patient-monitoring example illustrates how discrete physiological deviations can be mapped to transparent risk scores and personalized review schedules. The framework provides an auditable link between discrete stochastic dynamics, remaining-lifetime prediction, and condition-based intervention, while separating mathematical validation from clinical validation.

AI.tldr: Develops a finite-state first-passage framework for two-sided threshold crossings via a biased random walk with symmetric absorbing barriers, yielding survival/hazard formulas, ageing properties, remaining-life prediction, and optimal preventive-intervention scheduling.
AI.motivation: Discrete monitoring systems trigger intervention when values depart from an operating band, creating two-sided threshold crossings. Raw hitting times suffer from parity gaps, so there is a need for a rigorous finite-state framework that handles parity, ageing, and intervention timing.
AI.method: A biased random walk with symmetric absorbing barriers is analyzed through even- and odd-state Markov skeletons to define a parity-corrected lifetime. Adjacent-row likelihood-ratio inequalities verify monotonicity, establishing IFR and NBUE properties. Substochastic-matrix formulas give survival, hazard, mean lifetime, state-conditioned remaining useful life, and finite-horizon crossing risk. A renewal-cost criterion derives optimal preventive-intervention schedules. Parameters are matched via drift/variance matching to a two-point walk, with a rolling-window extension for nonstationarity.
AI.result: Ageing properties yield log-concave survival probabilities and geometric persistence bounds. Numerical experiments compare exact calculations with Monte Carlo, moment-matched inverse-Gaussian and Weibull benchmarks, serially correlated increments, calibration perturbations, and fixed-interval policies. A synthetic remote-patient-monitoring example maps discrete physiological deviations to risk scores and personalized review schedules.
AI.conclusion: The framework provides an auditable link between discrete stochastic dynamics, remaining-lifetime prediction, and condition-based intervention, while explicitly separating mathematical validation from clinical validation.

title: On the vortex filament conjecture for the Gross-Pitaevskii equation
summary: We establish one form of the vortex filament conjecture for the three-dimensional Gross-Pitaevskii equation. Given any smooth closed embedded binormal flow of curves on a compact time interval, we construct, in the small-core limit $\varepsilon\to0$, a family of exact solutions whose degree-one vortex filaments converge uniformly to the prescribed flow. Near the filament the solutions have the standard planar vortex profile, while away from it their phase gradients converge to the associated Biot-Savart field. We also derive a refined modulation law for the vortex filament.

AI.tldr: The paper proves a form of the vortex filament conjecture for the 3D Gross-Pitaevskii equation: for any smooth closed binormal flow, it constructs exact small-core solutions whose degree-one vortex filaments converge uniformly to the prescribed flow, with standard planar vortex profiles near the filament and Biot-Savart phase gradients away from it, plus a refined modulation law.
AI.motivation: The vortex filament conjecture predicts that vortex filaments in the 3D Gross-Pitaevskii equation evolve according to binormal flow, but a rigorous construction of solutions realizing arbitrary prescribed binormal flows was lacking.
AI.method: In the small-core limit ε→0, the authors construct a family of exact solutions associated to any smooth closed embedded binormal flow of curves on a compact time interval, controlling the vortex core profile and the far-field phase behavior.
AI.result: The constructed solutions have degree-one vortex filaments that converge uniformly to the prescribed binormal flow; near the filament they exhibit the standard planar vortex profile, and away from it their phase gradients converge to the associated Biot-Savart field. A refined modulation law for the vortex filament is also derived.
AI.conclusion: The result establishes one form of the vortex filament conjecture for the 3D Gross-Pitaevskii equation, rigorously linking prescribed binormal flows to exact vortex filament solutions in the small-core limit.

title: Counterexamples to Wang's Conjecture

AI.tldr: The paper disproves Wang's conjecture by constructing bounded Euclidean domains with principal curvatures greater than 1 on which a nonlinear Robin problem admits nonconstant positive solutions for a specific range of parameters.
AI.motivation: Wang's conjecture concerns conditions under which nonlinear Robin problems on domains with large principal curvatures admit only constant solutions. The paper aims to give a negative answer to this conjecture.
AI.method: For each n≥3, the authors exhibit ε>0 and δ∈(0,1) such that for q in (n/(n-2)−ε, n/(n-2)] and λ in (δ/(q−1), 1/(q−1)], they construct a bounded Euclidean domain Ω⊂ℝ^n with all principal curvatures bigger than 1 admitting a nonconstant positive solution.
AI.result: The construction yields, for every n≥3, domains Ω with principal curvatures greater than 1 on which the nonlinear Robin problem Δu=0 with boundary condition ∂u/∂ν+λu=u^q possesses a nonconstant positive solution.
AI.conclusion: Wang's conjecture is false: nonconstant positive solutions to the nonlinear Robin problem can exist on domains with large principal curvatures for suitable parameter ranges.

title: The Cauchy problem for Manton's Chern-Simons-Schrödinger equation
summary:
The Chern-Simons-Schrödinger equation (in the temporal gauge) arises as the Hamiltonian flow of the abelian Higgs energy on $\mathbb R^2$. Manton (arXiv:hep-th/9701027) introduced the equation as a model for the dynamics of the critical points of the energy, known as vortices. He conjectured that, for a certain range of coupling constants, the vortex motion under the Chern-Simons-Schrödinger flow can be effectively captured by a first-order ODE on the moduli space of self-dual vortices constructed by Jaffe-Taubes (1980) and Samols (1992).
  As a first step towards a rigorous proof of Manton's conjecture, we formulate the Cauchy problem in DeTurck gauge within the natural energy space and prove global well-posedness. We also obtain, as a corollary of the well-posedness theory and the stability results in our previous work (arXiv:2603.24900), orbital stability of the self-dual vortices under the Chern-Simons-Schrödinger flow near self-dual coupling. The heart of our analysis lies in developing a geometric Littlewood-Paley theory based on the covariant heat equation in caloric gauge, which we use to perform a paradifferential-style decomposition of the Chern-Simons-Schrödinger equation.

AI.tldr: The paper formulates the Cauchy problem for the Chern-Simons-Schrödinger equation in DeTurck gauge, establishing global well-posedness in the natural energy space as a step toward proving Manton's vortex dynamics conjecture.
AI.motivation: Manton conjectured that, for certain coupling constants, vortex motion under the Chern-Simons-Schrödinger flow is effectively described by a first-order ODE on the moduli space of self-dual vortices (Jaffe-Taubes, Samols). Rigorously proving this requires a foundational well-posedness theory, which the paper aims to provide as a first step.
AI.method: The authors formulate the Cauchy problem in DeTurck gauge within the natural energy space. Their core technical tool is a geometric Littlewood-Paley theory built on the covariant heat equation in caloric gauge, which enables a paradifferential-style decomposition of the Chern-Simons-Schrödinger equation.
AI.result: They prove global well-posedness of the Cauchy problem. As a corollary, combining with well-posedness theory and prior stability results, they obtain orbital stability of self-dual vortices under the Chern-Simons-Schrödinger flow near self-dual coupling.
AI.conclusion: The work establishes the analytical foundations needed for a rigorous proof of Manton's conjecture, and demonstrates orbital stability of self-dual vortices near self-dual coupling.

title: From $\mathrm{BV}^\mathcal A$ to $\mathrm{BV}$: An endpoint Korn estimate

title: Score-based Outlier Generation via Controlling the Radon-Nikodym Derivative
summary: Outliers are important for stress-testing algorithms and understanding system behaviour under rare conditions. Despite being commonly described as low-likelihood events, existing generative approaches rarely control likelihood explicitly. In this work, we introduce a measure-theoretic notion of outliers based on the distribution of log-likelihood values, which is guaranteed to assign higher probability mass to low-likelihood events with a specifiable magnitude. Building on this formulation, we derive how likelihood reweighting modifies the diffusion score and use this relation to motivate a controlled modification of the reverse-time dynamics. In particular, likelihood reweighting implies a scaling of the score function with a control term derived from the Radon-Nikodym derivative of the likelihood distributions. Correspondingly, the updated score function can be obtained with no retraining of the diffusion model. We exploit the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck semigroup underlying diffusion models to motivate an exponentially interpolated controller which approximates the true control. Experiments demonstrate controlled generation of low-likelihood samples while remaining consistent with the data geometry.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a measure-theoretic definition of outliers based on the distribution of log-likelihood values, and uses likelihood reweighting to controllably generate low-likelihood samples from diffusion models without retraining.
AI.motivation: Outliers are valuable for stress-testing algorithms and understanding rare-condition system behaviour, yet existing generative approaches rarely control likelihood explicitly, despite describing outliers as low-likelihood events.
AI.method: They define outliers measure-theoretically via the distribution of log-likelihood values, guaranteeing higher probability mass to low-likelihood events with a specifiable magnitude. They derive how likelihood reweighting modifies the diffusion score, scaling it by a control term from the Radon-Nikodym derivative of likelihood distributions. Using the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck semigroup, they motivate an exponentially interpolated controller approximating the true control, requiring no retraining.
AI.result: Experiments demonstrate controlled generation of low-likelihood samples while remaining consistent with the data geometry.
AI.conclusion: Likelihood reweighting provides a principled, training-free mechanism for controlled outlier generation in diffusion models, yielding samples that are both low-likelihood and geometrically faithful to the data.

title: Internal controllability of first order quasilinear hyperbolic systems with a reduced number of controls
summary: In this paper we investigate the exact controllability of $n \times n$ first order one-dimensional quasilinear hyperbolic systems by $m<n$ internal controls that are localized in space in some part of the domain. We distinguish two situations. The first one is when the equations of the system have the same speed. In this case, we can use the method of characteristics and obtain a simple and complete characterization for linear systems. Thanks to a linear test this also provides some sufficient conditions for the local exact controllability around the trajectories of semilinear systems. However, when the speed of the equations are not anymore the same, we see that we encounter the problem of loss of derivatives if we try to control quasilinear systems with a reduced number of controls. To solve this problem, as in a prior article by J.-M. Coron and P. Lissy on a Navier-Stokes control system, we first use the notion of algebraic solvability due to M. Gromov. However, in contrast with this prior article where a standard fixed point argument could be used to treat the nonlinearities, we use here a fixed point theorem of Nash-Moser type due to M. Gromov in order to handle the problem of loss of derivatives.

AI.tldr: The paper studies exact controllability of n×n one-dimensional first-order quasilinear hyperbolic systems using m<n spatially localized internal controls. It provides a complete characterization for the equal-speed (linear) case and sufficient conditions for semilinear local controllability, while the distinct-speed case is handled via algebraic solvability and a Nash-Moser fixed point argument to overcome loss of derivatives.
AI.motivation: Controlling hyperbolic systems with fewer controls than equations (m<n) is challenging, especially for quasilinear systems where loss of derivatives arises when speeds differ. The authors aim to extend controllability results to this reduced-control setting.
AI.method: Method of characteristics for the equal-speed case, yielding a linear test and sufficient conditions for semilinear local exact controllability; for the unequal-speed case, the notion of algebraic solvability (Gromov) combined with a Nash-Moser-type fixed point theorem to handle loss of derivatives.
AI.result: A simple, complete characterization for linear systems with equal speeds; sufficient conditions for local exact controllability of semilinear systems via a linear test; and a resolution of the loss-of-derivatives problem for quasilinear systems with distinct speeds using algebraic solvability and Nash-Moser.
AI.conclusion: Exact controllability with m<n localized internal controls is achievable: fully characterized in the equal-speed linear case and made tractable for quasilinear systems with distinct speeds via algebraic solvability and Nash-Moser techniques, extending ideas from Coron–Lissy's Navier-Stokes work.

title: Bernstein theorem for $3$-dimensional anisotropic minimal graphs with free boundary
summary: In this paper, we continue our recent study on anisotropic minimal surface equation with free boundary condition in Wang-Wei-Xia-Zhang (Arch Ration Mech Anal 250:42, 2026). The first main result solves the corresponding mixed boundary value problem. As an application, we prove the following Bernstein-type theorem: any anisotropic minimal graph over $\mathbb{R}^3_+$ with free boundary must be flat. These extend the classical results of Simon (Indiana Univ Math J 25:821--855, 1976; Math Z 154:265--273, 1977) to an appropriate free boundary setting.

AI.tldr: This paper solves a mixed boundary value problem for the anisotropic minimal surface equation with free boundary condition and proves a Bernstein-type theorem: any anisotropic minimal graph over R^3_+ with free boundary must be flat, extending Simon's classical results to a free boundary setting.
AI.motivation: The work continues recent study on the anisotropic minimal surface equation with free boundary condition, aiming to extend classical Bernstein-type results of Simon to an appropriate free boundary setting.
AI.method: The authors solve the mixed boundary value problem corresponding to the anisotropic minimal surface equation with free boundary condition, then apply this to derive a Bernstein-type rigidity result.
AI.result: The mixed boundary value problem is solved, and any anisotropic minimal graph over R^3_+ with free boundary is shown to be flat.
AI.conclusion: These results extend Simon's classical theorems (1976, 1977) to a free boundary setting for anisotropic minimal surfaces.

title: No free lunch for continuity of stochastic convolutions
summary:
We construct compact, exponentially stable $C_0$-semigroups $S$ on Hilbert spaces $X$ such that, for every $T>0$, the stochastic convolution $U_g(t)=\int_0^t S(t-s)g(s)\,\mathrm{d}β_s $ is unbounded on $[0,T]$ with positive probability for some predictable $g\in L^\infty(Ω;L^2(0,T;X))$, where $β$ is a real Brownian motion. One example is even an analytic semigroup. For the other, the negative generator $A$ has sectorial angle $π/2$ and a bounded $H^\infty$-calculus.
  Our main tool is a necessary condition: for exponentially stable semigroups, an $L^2$-maximal estimate on $\mathbb R_+$ forces a lower square-function estimate for the negative generator. We deduce this implication from a new identity involving the stochastic convolution, the subordinated Poisson semigroup, and a stopped Brownian motion. Combining this condition with Schauder multipliers on a conditional trigonometric basis yields counterexamples to the maximal estimate. An extrapolation argument then produces the integrands with unbounded stochastic convolutions.
  Finally, an energy-adapted chaining argument gives continuity and maximal estimates for arbitrary $C_0$-semigroups under the stronger condition $g\in L^2([0,T]; L^\infty(Ω;X))$.

AI.tldr: The authors construct compact, exponentially stable C0-semigroups on Hilbert spaces for which stochastic convolution can be unbounded with positive probability, refuting a general L2-maximal estimate for predictable integrands.
AI.motivation: To determine whether stochastic maximal L2-regularity/maximal estimates hold for general exponentially stable semigroups, and to identify the structural conditions that are actually necessary.
AI.method: Establish a necessary condition: for exponentially stable semigroups, an L2-maximal estimate on R+ forces a lower square-function estimate for the negative generator. Derive this from an identity relating stochastic convolution, subordinated Poisson semigroup, and stopped Brownian motion. Combine with Schauder multipliers on a conditional trigonometric basis to build counterexamples, then extrapolate to obtain unbounded stochastic convolutions. For positive results, use an energy-adapted chaining argument.
AI.result: Counterexamples: compact exponentially stable semigroups where, for every T>0, the stochastic convolution is unbounded on [0,T] with positive probability for some bounded predictable g. One example is analytic; another has negative generator with sectorial angle pi/2 and bounded H-infinity calculus. Positive result: continuity and maximal estimates for arbitrary C0-semigroups under the stronger condition g in L2([0,T]; Linf(Omega;X)).
AI.conclusion: L2-maximal estimates for stochastic convolutions do not hold for general exponentially stable semigroups, even analytic or H-infinity-calculus ones; the stronger Linf-in-space integrand condition restores maximal and continuity estimates.

title: Random field approximation and local counting statistics for the weakly interacting thermal Bose gas
summary: We study weakly interacting bosons on the three-dimensional torus at temperatures proportional to the critical temperature for Bose--Einstein condensation. We show that, as the expected particle number tends to infinity, the grand canonical Gibbs state is asymptotically described by the coherent state quantization of a random field that converges to a novel Bogoliubov random field. Moreover, the point process associated with the Gibbs state can be approximated by a Cox process. These results are based on and extend the approximation of the Gibbs state recently obtained by the first two authors and Nam. title: How turbulent flows grow vorticity at a point

summary: We describe how strong vorticity fluctuations appear in three-dimensional incompressible turbulence driven by a large-scale random force. By combining analytical and numerical methods, we construct a vorticity instanton: the most probable force history driving the flow to a prescribed large vorticity at a given point and time.
